80-office-of-religious-and-spiritual-lif: Links students to faith communities and liaisons, and gives space and resources to explore spirituality and live well in a pluralistic society. 3610 McTavish St., 3rd floor, Room 36-2.
80-office-for-sexual-violence-response-s: Confidential, non-judgmental support for students, faculty and staff of any gender affected by sexual or gender-based violence, in French and English. 550 Sherbrooke W., Suite 585, West Tower.
80-student-accessibility-and-achievement: Learning assessment, support and accommodations for students with documented disabilities, mental health issues, chronic illness or other impairments, whether temporary, permanent or episodic.
Main office: 1010 Sherbrooke W., Suite 410. Exam Centre: Redpath Library, 3459 McTavish, Suite RS-56. Macdonald: Centennial Centre, Room 124.
80-office-of-sustainability: Helps McGill become a model of sustainability, and helps you get involved or start a project. Sherbrooke 1010 Building, Suite 1200.
80-scholarships-and-student-aid-office: Bursaries, loans, Work Study, government aid and financial wellness workshops. Brown Building, East Wing, Suite 3200, and Centennial Centre, Room 124.
80-student-wellness-hub: Physical and mental health care for students who pay the Student Services fee: doctors, nurses, counsellors, access advisers, dietitians, psychiatrists by referral, sexologists, lab technicians, and the Healthy Living Annex.
Brown Building, 3rd floor, and Centennial Centre, Room 124.
81-macdonald-campus: Macdonald students can use services on both campuses, so say which when booking. Most are at Centennial Centre, Room 124, 21,111 Lakeshore Rd.
81-campus-life-and-engagement: Connects students to resources and opportunities, with a contact for incoming first-years.
81-career-planning-service-caps: Career education, events, advising, mentoring, workshops and the myFuture job board.
81-international-student-services-iss: Orientation, immigration and health insurance guidance, and support for Mastercard Foundation Scholars. Centennial Centre, Room 124. Write by webform or Insurance Portal ticket.
81-office-of-religious-and-spiritual-lif: Links students to faith communities and supports spiritual exploration.
81-scholarships-and-student-aid: Bursaries, loans, Work Study, government aid and financial wellness.
81-student-accessibility-and-achievement: Assessment, support and accommodations for documented disabilities, mental health issues and illness, with separate contacts for each campus.
81-student-wellness-hub: Health and wellness care for fee-paying students, including local wellness advisers. Macdonald clinic: Centennial Centre, Room 124.
82-office-for-sexual-violence-response-s: Confidential support for anyone affected by sexual or gender-based violence, in both languages.
82-office-of-sustainability: Based downtown, with monthly visits to Macdonald. Get involved or ask questions.
82-continuing-studies: Continuing Studies students don't pay Student Services fees but can opt in if registered for at least 9 credits in a term.
That gives access to CaPS, the Wellness Hub, International Student Services, Off-Campus Housing, MORSL and Student Accessibility. You need a McGill ID. Apply at Brown Building, Room 4100.
82-mcgill-athletics-package-for-continui: Membership covers the B2 Gym and drop-in basketball, badminton, jogging and lap swim, with classes extra. Currie Gym, 475 Pine Ave. W.
82-parking-for-continuing-studies-studen: Permits exist but space is limited. If you need to park close because of a disability, condition or injury, ask Student Accessibility.
82-university-centre-for-continuing-stud: Food and drink in the evening at the University Centre, 3480 McTavish St.
82-mcgill-writing-centre-tutorial-servic: In-person or virtual writing tutoring at every stage. See the MACES Tutorial Service page.
82-it-tools: See Resources for Students for what's available.
82-it-support: One place for help with email, Microsoft 365, Wi-Fi and VPN: knowledge base, service requests, chat, system status and tickets.
83-communication-and-collaboration: Tools that work together for your studies.
83-email: Every student gets a McGill address, usually firstname.lastname@mail.mcgill.ca. See p. 84.
83-ms-teams: Recommended for meetings, calls, messages and file sharing.
83-onedrive: 1 TB of free cloud storage for documents.
83-microsoft-office-and-365-apps: Install Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote and more on your own devices and sync with OneDrive, plus Forms, Sway, Stream and SharePoint. Not for those in short courses off the official transcript.
83-online-course-materials-and-lecture-r: myCourses has assignments, readings and syllabi. Many lectures are recorded for streaming, and Zoom is used when classes can't be on campus.
83-minerva: McGill's information system, with your username or ID and PIN.

Use it to apply and check status, see schedules and spaces, register and change courses, change programs (some faculties), see your unofficial transcript and degree evaluations, your username, Permanent Code, status and fees, update your details and preferred name, evaluate courses, apply for exchange (some faculties), apply to graduate, order transcripts, get tax receipts, and get proof for a reduced-fare STM Opus card.
83-secure-your-journey: Tips on strong passwords, 2FA, safe learning and phishing.
83-it-policies: McGill's IT resources are subject to its policies, listed on the IT policies site.
83-responsible-use-of-mcgill-information: The policy is a code of conduct for McGill technology. M.D.,C.M. and D.M.D. students also have social media guidelines.
83-report-security-incidents: Tell IT right away through the Service Desk or by phone. For bullying, harassment or safety risks, call Security Services: downtown 514-398-3000, Macdonald 514-398-7777.
84-use-of-cloud-services: The Cloud Directive governs online apps. Use approved ones; not all protect sensitive data.
84-two-factor-authentication-2fa: All accounts use 2FA for many systems, as required of Canadian higher education institutions, so a stolen password isn't enough.
84-email-communication: McGill email is the official channel, and you must check and act on it. Sign in on the Microsoft Office site, and confirm your address or set your password in Minerva's Personal Menu.
If you use another provider, see the IT Knowledge Base article. There's also a Policy on E-mail Communication with Students.
84-downtown-campus-athletics-and-recreat: Gym, fitness centre, varsity weight room, pool, fieldhouse, stadium, running tracks, tennis, squash, racquetball, spinning, fitness and martial arts studios, fields, training spaces, and gender-neutral changing rooms.

Join instructional, recreational, intramural and intercollegiate activities or sports clubs. Courses, intramurals, rentals and Fitness Centre have small fees. Skis, snowshoes, racquets and balls can be borrowed or rented. McGill Sports Complex, 475 Pine Ave. W.
84-macdonald-campus-athletics-and-recrea: Free gym, fitness centre, smart studios, multi-courts, fields, outdoor Trekfit gym and volleyball court, and green space. Intramurals and fitness courses cost a little, and equipment can be borrowed or rented. Offices: Stewart Athletic Complex.
85-ombudsperson-for-students: Confidential, independent, impartial help resolving disputes informally, with information, advice, intervention and referrals, before any formal process. 3610 McTavish St., Room 14.
85-extra-curricular-and-co-curricular-ac: Over 300 clubs and services: sports, charity and environment, outreach, arts and performance, health, languages and publications, hobbies, networking and leadership, activism, religion and culture.
85-co-curricular-activities: Learning outside class. Use myInvolvement, from CaPS, to find opportunities, and record them on your Co-Curricular Record.
85-university-centre-thomson-house-and-c: University Centre, 3480 McTavish: clubrooms, dining, ballroom, lounges and black box theatre. Thomson House, 3650 McTavish: graduate students. Macdonald: Centennial Centre. Space varies by season and health guidelines.
85-day-care: CPE McGill, 3491 Peel St.: independent, for 110 children aged four months to five years. Apply early at laplace0-5.com as places are limited.
Campus Day Care, 1 Maple Ave., Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue: independent, about 60 children of the same ages, with preference for the Macdonald community.
85-downtown-campus: McGill Campus Store, 680 Sherbrooke St. W.: books, stationery, clothing and gifts, plus a 24/7 online store and newsletter.
85-macdonald-campus: Centennial Centre, main floor: McGill and Macdonald clothing and insignia. Order online and pick up here.
87-about-the-faculty-of-agricultural-and: The Faculty and the School of Human Nutrition are on the Macdonald Campus: 650 hectares on the waterfront at the western tip of Montréal island, by public transport from downtown and the airport.

Degrees in agricultural sciences and applied biosciences, food and nutrition, environment, and bioresource engineering. Study abroad in places like Panama, Barbados or Africa, and internships are possible.

Labs, an experimental farm and the Morgan Arboretum. Known for plant and animal biotechnology, bioproducts, bioinformatics, food safety, environmental engineering, water, soils, parasitology, microbiology and ecosystem science. Small classes and hands-on learning.
87-mission: Excellence in teaching, research and service, so that food, health and natural resource needs are met while protecting the environment.
87-faculty-admission-requirements-and-ap: See the Undergraduate Admissions Guide for requirements and Key Academic Dates for deadlines. Apply online through Undergraduate Admissions.
Student Affairs Office, Macdonald Campus. Find your adviser with the site's search tool. For transfers, see Faculty Transfers and Programs.
88-faculty-information-and-regulations: Advisers help, but correct course choice, requirements and deadlines are your responsibility. Misunderstanding a rule won't earn an exemption.
88-minimum-credit-requirement: Your admission letter sets it. Usually 120 credits over four years, with up to 30 Advanced Standing for DCS, IB, French Baccalaureate, A-Levels or AP.
With a Québec DEC or equivalent: 90 credits, 113 for Bioresource Engineering, 115 for Dietetics, 122 for concurrent Food Science and Nutrition, plus any missing science.
From outside Québec with a high school diploma: start with the 30-credit Foundation Program. No credit for courses overlapping earlier work.
Transfers need 60 McGill credits, 72 for B.Eng.(Bioresource). B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and Diploma in Environment students take at least two-thirds of their credits in the Faculty.
88-minimum-grade-requirement: C or better in required, complementary and Foundation courses used for your program, and in prerequisites, unless the Chair agrees in writing.
88-academic-advisors: Before registering, see your program's academic adviser, who normally stays with you throughout. A faculty adviser in Student Affairs helps with record matters.
88-full-time-students: Full-time is at least 12 credits a term, normally 15, at most 18. Scholarships need 27 graded credits in Fall and Winter. Probationary: at most 14, unless the Committee allows more.
88-academic-standing: CGPA (or first-term TGPA) under 2.00 means Probationary, at most 14 credits. Then you need a TGPA of 2.50 to stay there or a CGPA of 2.00 to return; otherwise Unsatisfactory (Interim in Fall, under Probationary rules).
CGPA under 1.50 means Unsatisfactory, and you must withdraw (Interim in Fall). You can apply for readmission after at least one term away, not counting Summer.
When readmitted, reach CGPA 2.00 for Satisfactory or TGPA 2.50 for Probationary, or you must leave permanently. Dietetics has further standards (p. 118).
89-committee-on-academic-standing: Reviews special requests. Get the form at Student Affairs, Laird Hall 106.
89-credit-system: About three hours of work per credit each week, so nine hours for a 3-credit course.
89-school-of-continuing-studies-courses: Not all count toward your degree. Ask a faculty adviser before registering.
89-credit-transfer: Earlier courses are assessed after you accept your offer. Courses elsewhere while at McGill need permission first, and need a grade meeting the host's graduation standard. They don't count in GPA.
Exemptions need approval from the McGill instructor and your adviser. Full-time students may take courses at Québec universities through BCI with Student Affairs' approval, with at least a C.
Outside Québec, arrange an official transcript and submit everything within one month of finishing. IUT grades arrive automatically.
89-adding-a-second-major: Apply to the Associate Dean (Student Affairs), Laird Hall, Room 106, with CGPA 3.00+ and Satisfactory Standing, normally before finishing U1.
Propose all courses with each major's advisers. At least 36 credits must be unique to the second, approved by your adviser, Student Affairs and the other faculty. Each major's standards apply.
89-procedures-for-a-minor-program: Submit a Minor Approval Form, usually early in U2, to Student Affairs. It continues yearly until cancelled: tell the minor adviser and file a Program Change Form.
89-course-change-and-withdrawal-guidelin: See p. 34 and Important Dates. Student Affairs handles other changes.
90-graduate-courses-available-to-undergr: You need a CGPA of 3.2 and approval from Enrolment Services. They can't also count toward a graduate program. See Laird Hall 106.
90-attendance-and-conduct-in-class: The Dean handles teaching-related discipline. Professors may warn you about dishonest or improper conduct, and disciplinary cases go to the Associate Dean (Student Affairs). Be on time for everything.
90-examinations: See p. 62. The tentative schedule is posted about four weeks into term and the final one at six. Write in English or French, except language courses; oral presentations are in English.
90-reassessments-and-rereads: See the page on the McGill Exams site.
90-degree-requirements: C or better (or exemption) in all required and complementary courses, CGPA 2.00+, and all other requirements. Dietetics also needs the Stages with CGPA 3.00.
60 McGill credits, two-thirds in the Faculty for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.). B.Eng.(Bioresource): 72 McGill credits, of 143 in the program including Year 0.
90-scholarships-bursaries-prizes-and-med: Open to entering, in-course and graduating students with no application. See the Faculty's in-course scholarships page.
90-student-information: Staff can help with academics, residence, athletics, student life and health.
90-student-rights-and-responsibilities: Rules are published by the Dean of Students and the Secretariat.
90-the-student-affairs-office: Laird Hall, Room 106. Admissions, transfer credit, standing, exams, exchanges, transfers, program changes, registration, scholarships, second degrees and majors, minors, study away and graduation.
90-student-services: See p. 81. Eligible students can use services on both campuses.
90-macdonald-campus-residences: See p. 75, or the Student Housing site.
91-student-life: Undergraduate and FMT students belong to the Macdonald Campus Students' Society, which runs events, academic affairs and clubs. Graduate students have MCGSS, part of PGSS.
91-tuition-fees: See your e-bill and account summary in Minerva, and p. 44.
91-other-expenses: Budget at least $1,000, depending on your program, for textbooks and supplies. The Macdonald bookstore is open 10–5, Monday to Friday, with online orders for pickup. Food labs need uniforms; Nutrition students are told on acceptance or promotion.
91-immunization-for-dietetics-majors: Start and finish the Compulsory Immunization Program in Fall of U1, in Professional Practice Stage 1A. Bring your records to the health nurse. Later Stages require it complete, and updates may be needed.
91-language-requirement-for-professions: Québec orders, including those for agrologists, chemists, dietitians and engineers, require working French.
91-overview-of-programs-offered: Degrees: B.Eng.(Bioresource), B.Sc. in Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Food Science, Nutritional Sciences, and concurrent Food Science and Nutrition.

Also: Certificates in Ecological Agriculture and Food Science, Diploma in Environment, DCS in Farm Management and Technology, and M.Sc. and Ph.D. programs. Partner in the Bieler School of Environment.

Accreditation: Agricultural Economics and Sustainable Agricultural Systems (Ordre des agronomes and provincial institutes); Bioresource Engineering (professional engineer in any province and the Ordre des agronomes); Dietetics (Dietitians of Canada and ODNQ); Food Science (IFT and Ordre des chimistes). Dietetics practice takes place in teaching hospitals and other agencies.
91-bachelor-of-science-agricultural-and-: Pick one major and at least one specialization, or two for interdisciplinary interests, and optionally a minor. Environment majors pick a concentration, and Agricultural Economics specializations are for its own students.
Each specialization needs 18 credits that aren't shared with the major or the other, and 12 at the 400 level or higher. Honours versions are open after U2 if you qualify.
92-majors-and-honours: Graduates of asterisked programs may qualify for the Ordre des agronomes du Québec and provincial institutes.
92-specializations: Usually 24 credits forming a package to prepare you for a discipline. Choose one, or two to broaden. Ask your adviser about others.
92-bieler-school-of-environment: A joint initiative with Arts and Science, offering programs you can take on both campuses (p. 821).
92-environmental-programs-on-the-macdona: Interdepartmental programs in the B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Eng.(Bioresource), for training in an interdisciplinary subject and managing natural resources.
93-exchange-programs: All McGill exchanges, plus Faculty-specific ones (p. 1289).
93-internship-opportunities: Hands-on work placements tailored by your employer and instructor.
93-faes-200-faes-300-internship-program: Full-time undergraduates with CGPA 2.7+: at least 10 weeks at 35 hours a week, related to your field. FAES 200 is pass/fail with no credit; FAES 300 is 3 credits, graded.
93-agri-310-internship-in-agriculture-en: 3 credits, at least 12 weeks, in a business in your field, to understand its technical, economic and social challenges.
93-agri-410d1-d2-agrology-internship: At least 420 hours, part of the Professional Agrology Specialization and required training for the Ordre des agronomes. Placements need the instructor's approval.
93-agri-499-agricultural-development-int: Supervised practical work on agriculture and international development: abroad, with an agency, or on research. Placements need the instructor's approval.
93-graduate-programs-in-agricultural-and: M.Sc., M.Sc. Applied and Ph.D. through Animal Science, Bioresource Engineering, Food Science, Human Nutrition, Natural Resource Sciences, Parasitology and Plant Science. Graduate office: Macdonald-Stewart Building.
94-browse-academic-units-and-programs: Degrees: B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.), B.Sc.(F.Sc.), B.Sc.(Nutr.Sc.), B.Eng.(Bioresource) and the concurrent B.Sc. Also post-baccalaureate certificates in Food Science and Ecological Agriculture, and a Diploma in Environment. Bieler offers further programs (p. 821).
94-foundation-program: At least 30 credits of basic math and science, for those entering from outside Québec's CEGEP system, leading to any of the Faculty's degrees.
DCS, AP, A-Levels, IB, French Baccalaureate, placement exams and other studies can bring exemptions or credits; ask Student Affairs.
95-program-description: Core science prerequisites for students coming from high school outside CEGEP.
95-required-courses-27-credits: Plus a 3-credit elective, chosen with your adviser.
96-degree-requirements-b-sc: To graduate, you need both the program's courses and the degree's requirements, including Foundation and structure (p. 1106). Fitting them together is your responsibility, and SOUSA's Degree Planning Guide helps.
98-about-the-department-of-animal-scienc: For interests from livestock nutrition, breeding, reproduction and welfare to animal health and biotechnology models of human disease.
Offers Animal Biology and Health, Livestock, and Global Food Security specializations, taken within a major.
To become a professional agrologist, take the Sustainable Agricultural Systems Major with Livestock and 9 credits in Professional Agrology.
98-program-description: Basic biology of large mammals and birds, giving a background in biomedical studies and animal models. Prepares you for most North American veterinary colleges, graduate biology and lab work.
Not open to B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) students, who can take the specialization instead.
98-program-description-2: Livestock production essentials: reproduction, breeding and genomics, nutrition, welfare, farm experience and precision agriculture, in a global context.
Pairs with the Sustainable Agricultural Systems Major, and Professional Agrology content can lead to Ordre des agronomes eligibility.
